findings.title: Doc says an old host's 404 "stays quiet", but only Sentry is skipped
findings.body: The new sentence sits in a list of routes whose "HTTP 409 responses are dropped", and adds `GET /api/v1/agents/:id/skills` to it. That route never answers 409. The case the PR targets is a remote host that predates the route and answers 404. `expectedProbeConflict` (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts:293-295`) requires `status === 409`, so `reportResponseError` (`:336`) still calls `reportApiError`. That call emits the `ao.requests.failed` analytics event (`:311`), once per 30 s. The Sentry capture is the only thing skipped (`:317`). So the 404 is not quiet, and it is not "dropped" like the 409s in the same list. The comment at `api-client.ts:288-289` and the `EXPECTED_PROBE_CONFLICTS` heading ("Conversation probes that 409", `:280`) have the same mismatch. Either say that the old-host 404 is still counted as an analytics event and only kept out of Sentry, or make `expectedProbeConflict` accept 404 for this operation, if the goal is for it to be dropped entirely.

contracts.action: New chat page fetches GET /api/v1/agents/{agent}/skills and merges it into the "/" menu
contracts.equivalent_path: Live session skills via GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation/skills (conversations_skills.go) and readChatSkills cache
contracts.before_after: Before: the menu showed only the list a past session of this agent reported (readChatSkills), empty on a first chat. Now: that list stays first and scanned skills not already in it are appended (mergeChatSkills). The scan reuses conversationSkillsResponse and withSkillMetadata, so the DTO and display metadata match the session path.
contracts.visible_effect: The "/" menu lists skills on a first chat. Skills appear after the query resolves, and the result is cached for 30 s per host, agent and project.
contracts.failure_mode: The query has retry:false and the hook returns NO_SKILLS on error. The menu falls back to the reported list and no error is shown. An old remote host's 404 is kept out of Sentry but still emits an analytics event (see finding).

contracts.action: Controller resolves projectId to a workspace path and scans skill folders on the host
contracts.equivalent_path: Other controllers that read a project through projectsvc.Manager.Get
contracts.before_after: The new path ignores any Get error, a nil result project, and FolderMissing, and falls back to scanning the user's folders only. It returns 200 even when the project cannot be resolved. A transient PROJECT_LOAD_FAILED is therefore indistinguishable from "no project skills", and the client caches that for 30 s.
contracts.visible_effect: The list may silently lack project skills while the project store fails, which fits the stated Scratchpad and standalone design.
contracts.failure_mode: Only user-level skills are returned. No log line records the swallowed error. The only reader is the loopback or authenticated API with Manager.Get, and agentID is matched against a fixed harness switch, so no path traversal is possible. Project-controlled settings.json can only enable plugins already listed in the user's installed_plugins.json.

summary:
I found one problem, a docs and comment mismatch. I read every file in this part and the unchanged code it relies on: `skill_metadata.go`, `conversations_skills.go`, the project `Manager.Get` and `GetResult`, and `api-client.ts` error reporting. Nothing else turned up, and no blockers.

The new backend skill scan, the controller's project lookup, the OpenAPI and `schema.ts` additions, and the frontend query and merge logic are consistent with the existing session skills path.

The finding is in `docs/telemetry.md`. It says a remote host too old to have the new route "stays quiet", but the old host's 404 is only kept out of Sentry and still emits an `ao.requests.failed` analytics event. The comment in `api-client.ts` carries the same mismatch.

Two smaller things I did not report:
- The OpenAPI spec documents a 500 response that the handler never returns.
- `agents_skills_test.go` does not cover the `FolderMissing` branch.

I did not run any code or tests."
